Cheapest fix candidates are already written into the trouble's the_fix_when_taken, ordered: (a) a corpus-wide chain census as a standing tooth or probe, so a break is found in minutes rather than eight days and by design rather than incidentally — this is the layer that was missing, since the chain detected everything and told nobody; (b) a date floor on adopt_chain so it refuses to adopt an entry newer than the adoption itself; (c) run_proof persists through the door itself, which is the option the ORIGINAL 2026-07-30 report named and which was not taken. open_threads: LIVE TROUBLE, prior_attempts 1 — 'the single write-door for the validation trail is not the only path to the file' was cleared 2026-08-05 with three physics layers and DID NOT HOLD. Measured 2026-08-15: six trails carry seven entries with no trail_link, dated 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-08, from two voyages (sail:banding-berths-at-the-general-level, and ticket the-inference-proxy-is-a-rules-stack which wrote five inside 66 seconds). Every one carries exactly the ratified eight fields and exactly run_proof's evidence keys — so it is run_proof's output written to the file by a hand that was not the door. Why each layer missed it: the MODE BIT cannot protect a file that does not yet exist (3 of 7 are entry 0 of a trail created in that same commit) and otherwise is defeated by any writer that replaces the inode by rename, which is the door's OWN technique; the CORPUS SCAN censuses modules and an ad-hoc script is not a module (the original 2026-07-30 occurrence was an ad-hoc script too); the CHAIN worked and was the only layer that did, but nothing reads it corpus-wide, so the breach sat eight days and surfaced only when a clearance check happened to consult one trail. NOTHING WAS RECOVERABLE — git shows each entry arrived unlinked and carries no link at any commit. NOTHING WAS ADOPTED, EDITED OR CHMOD'D. RIDING FINDING: adopt_chain cannot tell this from prehistory — it refuses a link that fails to verify but a MISSING link passes straight through, so it would silently mint links over a post-door bypass and erase the evidence its own docstring says it exists to preserve; the distinguisher is the date and nothing reads it. NOT A FINDING, recorded so nobody re-derives it: cairn/tools/base/validations/test_nest.json is mode 664 where the other 89 are 444 — the 2026-08-05 clearing note already predicted this ('a fresh clone lands these files at 0644'), so it is expected residue; left untouched deliberately, since chmod by hand would be a hand applying physics. CHART-LEG FALSIFICATIONS from this voyage (findings about the chart, not lapses of attention): survey held resolve()'s meter row but not that resolver is a required injected argument; survey described the Transport recorder but not that its get shares the urls list with post (this cost the first proof run a red); TesterDevice's home is device.py not tester.py and was outside every berth's holdings; and no berth held the gated_by requirement, the forwarding-order obligation, or the fact that history/state are .json at this address. TOOL-CALL SCORE, honestly coarse: the count is the packet's score read downward, and this voyage spans a compaction boundary so no exact figure survives — the post-compaction close alone took ~22 calls and the voyage overall well exceeded 100. That is a coarse measurement to sharpen, not an absence of one; ticket the-builds-tool-calls-are-evidence-about-the-chart is where the observer that would make it exact lives.
